entries.reason: DATA-001 matches the SSH user in the scp-style git remotes used as test fixtures in governance_id_test.go. That user is the conventional one every git forge accepts, not a person's address. The fixtures exist because the parser must reduce an scp-style remote to the same identity as the https form, and that branch splits on the last colon, so it cannot be tested without the user-at-host shape. Rewriting the literal to dodge the pattern would leave a fixture that no longer resembles the remotes it stands for. Worded without quoting a remote, because an earlier version of this reason quoted one and the baseline file was then flagged by the same rule.

Same fixture shape already reviewed for governance_id_test.go: DATA-001 matches the SSH user in an scp-style git remote used as a test fixture. That user is the conventional one every git forge accepts, not a person's address. The fixture exists because the outcome tracker must reduce every remote spelling to one identity — otherwise the same repository is keyed twice depending on how it was cloned — and the scp branch splits on the last colon, so it cannot be tested without the user-at-host shape. Rewriting the literal to dodge the pattern would leave a fixture that no longer resembles the remotes it stands for. Worded without quoting a remote, because quoting one causes this file to be flagged by the same rule.
